title: Saturday talent contests at the Empress Theater
summary: Kids performed before the Saturday movie for free admission; Wes and June played while Monk strummed a guitar without playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And I remember another period where we worked at...on a Saturday at the Empress Theater, we had a thing every Saturday afternoon, was a contest. And that meant that before the movie started -- cowboys and the whole thing, you know, cowboys and cartoons on Saturday -- all the kids would come in and they could line up to be in the contest, to perform on stage, before the movie started. So all the ones that performed got in free. So this was like a free ticket, a free way in to the show.
Now, we'd talk among ourselves and get a little group together to go down and play, see. Wes could play, and my older brother June could play.
I remember I had a...I can't even remember where this guitar came from, but there was a guitar, and I was strumming it as if I was playing.
No! No, you know, I wasn't...

No, it was a fun thing. It was just a free way to get in the show. Because there were other kids perhaps ten times worse than we were. But to get on the stage and perform, just being on that stage, it was great. And the ones in the audience would...were just enjoying a bunch of clowns on the stage.
